title: Psalm 47: God Is King of All the Earth
summary: All the peoples are called to clap and shout to God, because the LORD Most High is the great King over all the earth. He has given Israel its inheritance, and he has ascended amid shouts and the sound of the horn. The psalm calls again and again for praise, and it ends with the nobles of the nations gathered as the people of the God of Abraham.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 47
from.text: It is one of the enthronement psalms, a group (usually 47, 93, and 95 to 99) that celebrate the LORD as king.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 47
from.text: The two halves follow the typical pattern of a hymn

line: All peoples are called to clap and shout, because the LORD Most High is King over all the earth; it ends with the nobles of the nations gathered as the people of the God of Abraham.
guide: The hope here is not that one people wins and others lose, but that all of them end up praising the same King. Not every prayer is quiet; praise God aloud with others.

stanzas.title: Clap and shout: the great King chooses his people
God reigns, and the nations gather to him

verses.t: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph.
How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!
He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah
God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn.
Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!
For God is King of all the earth; sing profound praises to Him.
God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne.
The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.
